headline: Salahuddin praises President Shahabuddin's role in constitutional continuity
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed says the outgoing president played a critical role between August 5 and 8, 2024, to keep the state on a constitutional path.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has praised former President Mohammed Shahabuddin for his role in maintaining constitutional continuity during a critical transition period.
Salahuddin stated that Shahabuddin's actions between August 5 and August 8, 2024, before the formation of the interim government, were very important for the state.
While acknowledging that Shahabuddin was elected under a fascist and autocratic government and faced criticism, the Home Minister noted that he cooperated with the current government.
The BNP views the presidency as a constitutional institution and believes the former president carried out his duties with proper dignity during his tenure.
President Shahabuddin has resigned, submitting his resignation letter to the speaker under constitutional rules, which will now be published in a gazette.
According to Salahuddin, the president may resign for health reasons or any other reason, and the process has been handled according to procedure.
The Election Commission will now take steps to elect a new president, with the presidential election required to be held within 90 days.
Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad will carry out the duties of the acting president until a new president is elected.
caption:
He was elected under a 'mafia government,' but did he save the state's constitutional path? Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed weighs in.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has praised former President Mohammed Shahabuddin for his role in maintaining constitutional continuity during a critical transition period.

Salahuddin stated that Shahabuddin's actions between August 5 and August 8, 2024, before the formation of the interim government, were very important for the state.

While acknowledging that Shahabuddin was elected under a fascist and autocratic government and faced criticism, the Home Minister noted that he cooperated with the current government.

The BNP views the presidency as a constitutional institution and believes the former president carried out his duties with proper dignity during his tenure.

President Shahabuddin has resigned, submitting his resignation letter to the speaker under constitutional rules, which will now be published in a gazette.

According to Salahuddin, the president may resign for health reasons or any other reason, and the process has been handled according to procedure.

The Election Commission will now take steps to elect a new president, with the presidential election required to be held within 90 days.

Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad will carry out the duties of the acting president until a new president is elected.

#Bangladesh #Politics #President #ConstitutionalContinuity #BNP

Source: Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star, Somoy News, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo

headline: Man arrested after harassing CU student on bus and returning to target her
summary: A Chittagong University student filed a case after a man allegedly harassed her and then tracked the bus to continue the intimidation.
details: A female student of Chittagong University (CU) has filed a case alleging she was sexually harassed by a fellow passenger on a bus bound for Khagrachhari.
The student reports that the man, identified as Mohammad Jasim, touched her under the pretext of throwing away a cigarette while she was sitting by the window.
When she protested, the accused allegedly began verbally abusing and threatening her, leading other passengers to intervene and force him off the bus in Hathazari.
In a shocking turn, the accused allegedly took a CNG-run auto-rickshaw to catch up with the bus at a stop in Fatikchhari, boarding it again to continue the harassment.
Passengers and bus staff eventually detained the man and handed him over to the Fatikchhari Police Station.
A case has been filed under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act, and the Officer-in-Charge of Fatikchhari Police Station confirmed that legal proceedings are underway.
caption:
He was forced off the bus for harassing a student—then he chased the bus in an auto-rickshaw to do it again.

A female student of Chittagong University (CU) has filed a case alleging she was sexually harassed by a fellow passenger on a bus bound for Khagrachhari.

The student reports that the man, identified as Mohammad Jasim, touched her under the pretext of throwing away a cigarette while she was sitting by the window.

When she protested, the accused allegedly began verbally abusing and threatening her, leading other passengers to intervene and force him off the bus in Hathazari.

In a shocking turn, the accused allegedly took a CNG-run auto-rickshaw to catch up with the bus at a stop in Fatikchhari, boarding it again to continue the harassment.

Passengers and bus staff eventually detained the man and handed him over to the Fatikchhari Police Station.

A case has been filed under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act, and the Officer-in-Charge of Fatikchhari Police Station confirmed that legal proceedings are underway.
